name: Na'ama (Sofar's hometown Na'ama, not a person but a place name associated with Job's friend Sofar)
title: Place name associated with Sofar the Na'amathite
summary: Na'ama is not a biblical person but a place name used to identify Sofar, one of Job's three friends, who is called "the Na'amathite" (from Na'ama). The place Na'ama is likely a city in northwestern Arabia or in the region of Edom. Sofar from Na'ama is known for his speeches in the book of Job, where he argues that Job's suffering is due to sin.

keyEvents.title: Sofar the Na'amathite introduced
keyEvents.description: Sofar from Na'ama is mentioned as one of Job's three friends who came to comfort him in his suffering.

keyEvents.title: Sofar's first speech
keyEvents.description: Sofar the Na'amathite delivers his first speech, rebuking Job and claiming that God is punishing him for hidden sin.

keyEvents.title: Sofar urges Job to repent
keyEvents.description: Sofar from Na'ama urges Job to turn to God with a pure heart, promising that this will lead to restoration.

keyEvents.title: Zophar's Second Speech
keyEvents.description: In his second speech, Zophar the Naamathite describes the fate of the wicked and claims that their prosperity is short-lived.

keyEvents.title: God Rebukes Job's Friends
keyEvents.description: God speaks to Eliphaz and includes Zophar from Naamah among the three friends who have not spoken rightly about Him, and tells them to offer burnt offerings.
